images.title: One roti, more sharers
images.purpose: Pose the opening question: when the same roti is shared equally by more children, how big is one share?
images.composition: Two equal round rotis side by side with wide space between them, and one short question line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one round roti cut by one straight line through the centre into 2 equal pieces, one piece filled teal #0072B2, the other plain. Right: one round roti of exactly the same size cut by two straight lines through the centre into 4 equal pieces, one piece filled amber #E69F00, the others plain. No numbers or fractions on any piece. Below, centred: one question line. Exactly 2 rotis, 2 coloured pieces, 1 question line.

images.takeaway: One roti, shared by more children: how big is each share?
images.description: Two same-size rotis: one cut into 2 equal pieces with one piece shaded teal, one cut into 4 equal pieces with one piece shaded amber, under the question which share is bigger.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one child's share in each roti and guess which is bigger, without naming any fraction yet.

image_decisions.why: The opening question is about the size of shares of one roti, which a picture of two cut rotis poses at a glance.
